text: A power transmission line feeds input power at 2300 V to a step down transformer with its primary windings having 4000 turns. The output power is delivered at 230 V by the transformer. If the current in the primary of the transformer is 5A and its efficiency is 90%, the output current would be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

Primary voltage $(V_{P}) = 2300 V$

Primary current $(I_{P}) = 5A$

Secondary voltage $(V_{S}) = 230 V$

efficiency ($η$) = 90%

We know,

Efficiency ($η$) = $\frac{\mathrm{Sec}ondaryPower}{\mathrm{Pr}imaryPower}$

$\therefore$   $η$ = $\frac{P_{S}}{P_{P}}$ = $\frac{V_{S}I_{S}}{V_{P}I_{P}}$

$\Rightarrow$   0.9 = $\frac{230\times \mathrm{I}_{S}}{2300\times 5}$

$\Rightarrow$   I = 45 A
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text: The energy associated with electric field is $(U_{E})$ and with magnetic field is $(U_{B})$ for an electromagnetic wave in free space. Then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Energy density of magnetic field $(U_{B}) =$ $\frac{B^{2}}{2μ_{0}}$

Also, 

Energy density  of electric field 

$U_{E} =$ $\frac{1}{2}$ $ε_{0}E^{2}$

= $\frac{1}{2}$ $ε_{0}$ $B^{2} C^{2}$       [as    $\frac{E}{B}$ = C ]

= $\frac{1}{2}$ $ε_{0}$ $B^{2}$ $\times$ $\left (\frac{1}{ε_{0}μ_{0}}\right )$    [as   $C^{2} =$ $\frac{1}{ε_{0}μ_{0}}$]

=  $\frac{B^{2}}{2μ_{0}}$

$\therefore$  $U_{B} = U_{E}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text: A force acts on a 2 kg object so that its position is given as a function of time as $x = 3t^{2} + 5$. What is the work done by this force in first 5 seconds ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Displacement, 

$x = 3t^{2} + 5$

$\therefore$  v = $\frac{dx}{dt}=6t$

At  t = 0,   velocity = 6 $\times$ 0 = 0

at  t = 5, velocity = 5 $\times$ 6 = 30 m/s

we  know from work energy theorem,

Work (W) = change in kinetic energy ($\Delta$K)

= $\frac{1}{2}mv_{F}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}mv_{i}^{2}$

=  $\frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ 2 $\times$ $(30)^{2}$  $-$ 0

= 900 J
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text: A particle having the same charge as of electron moves in a circular path of radius 0.5 cm under the influence of a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If an electric field of 100 V/m makes it to move in a straight path, then the mass of the particle is (Given charge of electron = 1.6 $\times$ $10^{-19} C)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, 

radius of circular path(r) = 0.5 cm

Magnetic field (B) = 0.5 T

Electric field (E) = 100 V/m

Charge of particle (q) = 1.6$\times10^{-19} C$

As particle is moving in a circular path so,

$\frac{mv^{2}}{r}=qvB$

$\Rightarrow$  r = $\frac{mv}{qB}$ . . . . . . . (1)

When electric field of 100 v/m is applied on the particle then particle is moving in the straight line. So, the net force on the particle is zero.

$\therefore$    $F_{$net} = 0

$\Rightarrow$   $F_{e} = F_{m}$

$\Rightarrow$  qE = qvB

$\Rightarrow$   E = vB  . . . . .(2)

From equation (1) and (2) we get,

r = $\frac{m}{qB}\left (\frac{E}{B}\right )$

= $\frac{mE}{qB^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$   m = $\frac{qB^{2}r}{E}$

=  $\frac{1.6\times 10^{-19}\times (0.5)^{2}\times 0.5\times 10^{-2}}{100}$

= 2 $\times$ $10^{-24} kg$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text: Expression for time in terms of G (universal gravitational constant), h (Planck constant) and c (speed of light) is proportional to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let t $\propto$ $G^{x} h^{y} c^{z}$

$\therefore$   [t] = [G]$^{x}$  [h]$^{y}$  [c]$^{z}$    . . . . . (1)

We know, 

F = $\frac{GM^{2}}{R^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$  G = $\frac{FR^{2}}{M^{2}}$

$\therefore$  [G] = $\frac{\left [MLT^{-2}\right ]\left [L^{2}\right ]}{[M^{2}]}$

[G] = $[M^{-1}L^{3}T^{-2}]$

Also,

E = hf

$\therefore$  [h] = $\frac{[E]}{[f]}$

= $\frac{\left [ML^{2}T^{-2}\right ]}{[T^{-1}]}$

= $\left [ML^{2}T^{-1}\right ]$

[C] = $\left [M^{o}LT^{-1}\right ]$

From equation (1) we get, 

$\left [M^{o}L^{o}T^{1}\right ]=\left [M^{-1}\qquad L^{3}T^{-2}\right ]^{x}\left [M\quad L^{2}T^{-1}\right ]^{y}\left [M^{o}LT^{-1}\right ]^{z}$

$\left [M^{o}L^{o}T^{1}\right ]=\left [M^{-x+y}L^{3x+2y+z}T^{-2x-y-z}\right ]$

By comparing the power of M, L, T

$-$ x + y = 0

$\Rightarrow$  x = y

3x + 2y + z = 0

$\Rightarrow$  5x + z = 0 . . . . .                  (2)

$-$ 2x $-$ y $-$ z = 1

$\Rightarrow$  $-$ 3x $-$ z = 1  . . . . (3)

By solving (2) and (3), we get,

x = $\frac{1}{2}$ = y  and z = $-$ $\frac{5}{2}$

$\therefore$  t $\propto$ $\sqrt{\frac{Gh}{C^{5}}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text: The energy required to take a satellite to a height 'h' above Earth surface (radius of Earth = 6.4 $\times$ $10^{3} km)$ is $E_{1}$ and kinetic energy required for the satellite to be in a circular orbit at this height is $E_{2}$. The value of h for which $E_{1}$ and $E_{2}$ are equal, is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Energy required to move a satellite from earth surface to height h is, 

$E_{1} = U_{h}$ $-$ $U_{$surface}

= $-$ $\frac{GMm}{R+h}-\left (-\frac{GMm}{R}\right )$

= GMm $\left (\frac{1}{R}-\frac{1}{R+h}\right )$

= $\frac{GMm}{R(R+h)}\times h$

We know, for satellite at height h.

Centrifugal force = Gravitational force 

$\Rightarrow$  $\frac{mv^{2}}{R+h}=\frac{GMm}{(R+h)^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$  $mv^{2}$ = $\frac{GMm}{R+h}$

$\therefore$   $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$ = $\frac{GMm}{2(R+h)}$

$\therefore$  Kinetic energy $(E_{2}) =$ $\frac{GMm}{2(R+h)}$

Given that,

$E_{1} = E_{2}$

$\therefore$  $\frac{GMm}{R(R+h)}\times h=\frac{GMm}{2(R+h)}$

$\Rightarrow$  $\frac{h}{R}=\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$  h = $\frac{R}{2}$

$\therefore$  h = $\frac{6.4\times 10^{3}}{2}$

= 3.2 $\times$ $10^{3} km$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text: A series AC circuit containing an inductor (20 mH), a capacitor (120 $μ$F) and a resistor (60 $\Omega$) is driven by an AC source of 24V/50 Hz. The energy dissipated in the circuit in 60 s is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Energy dissipated in 60 Sec 

$= (P_{$avg}) $\times$ 60

$= V_{$rms} $\times$ $I_{$rms} $\times$ cos$𝜙$ $\times$ 60

$= V_{$rms} $\times$ $\frac{V_{rms}}{Z}\times$ cos$𝜙$ $\times$ 60

$X_{L} =$ $ω$L = 2$π$FL

= 2$π$(50)$\times$ 20 $\times$ $10^{-3}$

= 2$π$ $\Omega$

$X_{C} =$ $\frac{1}{ωC}$

= $\frac{1}{2πfC}$

= $\frac{1}{2π(50)\times 120\times 10^{-6}}$

= 26.52 $\Omega$

$\therefore$   $X_{C}$ $-$ $X_{L} = 20.24$ $\simeq$ 20

$\therefore$   Z = $\sqrt{(X_{C}-X_{L})^{2}+R^{2}}$

= $\sqrt{(20)^{2}+60^{2}}$

= 20  $\sqrt{10}$ $\Omega$

Also cos$𝜙$ = $\frac{R}{Z}$ = $\frac{60}{20\sqrt{10}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}$

$\therefore$   Energy dissipated in 60 sec

= $\frac{(24)^{2}}{20\sqrt{10}}\times \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\times 60$

= 5.17 $\times$ $10^{2} J$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text: One of the two identical conducting wires of length L is bent in the form of a circular loop and the other one into a circular coil of N identical turns. If the same current is passed in both, the ratio of the magnetic field at the centre of the loop $(B_{L})$ to that at the center of the coil $(B_{C}),  i.e$. $\frac{B_{L}}{B_{C}}$ will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


For loop,

L = 2$π$R

For coil,

L = N $\times$ 2$π$r

$\therefore$   2$π$R = N $\times$ 2$π$r

$\Rightarrow$  R = Nr

$\Rightarrow$  r = $\frac{R}{N}$

We know, 

$B_{L} =$ $\frac{μ_{0}i}{2R}$

and  $B_{C} = N$ $\times$ $\frac{μ_{0}i}{2r}$

$\therefore$  $\frac{B_{L}}{B_{C}}=\frac{\frac{μ0i}{2R}}{N\times \frac{μ0i}{2\left (\dfrac{R}{N}\right )}}=\frac{1}{N^{2}}$

text: A rod of mass 'M' and length '2L' is suspended at its middle by a wire. It exhibits torsional oscillations; If two masses each of 'm' are attached at distance 'L/2' from its centre on both sides, it reduces the oscillation frequency by 20%. The value of ratio m/M is close to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Initially :


[IMG]


After putting 2 masses of each 'm' at a distance $\frac{L}{2}$ from center : 


[IMG]


We know,

Time period (T) = 2$π$ $\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{I}}{C}}$

$\therefore$  T $\propto$ $\sqrt{\mathrm{I}}$

$\therefore$   Frequency (f) $\propto$ $\sqrt{\frac{1}{\mathrm{I}}}$

$\therefore$   $\frac{f_{1}}{f_{2}}$ = $\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{I}_{2}}{\mathrm{I}_{1}}}$

Also given that, 

After putting two masses 'm' at both end new frequency becomes 80% of initial frequency.

$\therefore$   $f_{2} = 0.8f_{1}$

$\therefore$   $\frac{f_{1}}{0.8f_{1}}$ = $\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{I}_{2}}{\mathrm{I}_{1}}}$

$\therefore$   $\frac{\mathrm{I}_{1}}{\mathrm{I}_{2}}$ = 0.64

Initial moment of inertia of the system, 

$\mathrm{I}_{1}$ = $\frac{M(2L)^{2}}{12}$

Final moment of inertia of the system, 

$I_{2} =$ $\frac{M(2L)^{2}}{12}$ + 2$\left (m\left (\frac{L}{2}\right )^{2}\right )$

$\therefore$   $\frac{M(2L)^{2}}{12}$ = 0.64 $\left [\frac{ML^{2}}{3}+\frac{mL^{2}}{2}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{ML^{2}}{3\times 0.64}$ = $\frac{ML^{2}}{3}$ + $\frac{mL^{2}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{M}{1.92}-\frac{M}{3}=\frac{m}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{1.08M}{3\times 1.92}$ = $\frac{m}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{m}{M}$ = $\frac{1.08\times 2}{3\times 1.92}$ = 0.37

text: Charge is distributed within a sphere of radius R with a volume charge density $ρ(r)=\frac{A}{r^{2}}e^{-2r/a},$ where A and a are constants. If Q is the total charge of this charge distribution, the radius R is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Volume of this spherical layer,

dv = (4$πr^{2})dr$

charge present in this layer, 

dq = $ρ$ (4$πr^{2} dr)$

=  $\frac{A}{r^{2}}e^{-\frac{2r}{a}}\left (4πr^{2}dr\right )$

= $Ae^{-\frac{2r}{a}}(4πdr)$

$\therefore$  Total charge in the sphere,

Q= $\int\limits _{0}^{R}4πAe^{-\frac{2r}{a}}dr$

= 4$π$A$\int\limits _{0}^{R}e^{-\frac{2r}{a}}dr$

= 4$π$A$\left [\frac{e^{-\dfrac{2r}{a}}}{-\frac{2}{a}}\right ]_{0}^{R}$

= 4$π$A $\left (-\frac{a}{2}\right )\left (e^{-\frac{2R}{a}}-1\right )$

$\therefore$  Q = 2$π$aA $\left (1-e^{-\frac{2R}{a}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$  $1-e^{-\frac{2R}{a}}$ = $\frac{Q}{2πaA}$

$\Rightarrow$  $e^{-\frac{2R}{a}}$ = 1 $-$ $\frac{Q}{2πaA}$

$\Rightarrow$  $e^{\frac{2R}{a}}$ = $\frac{1}{1-\frac{Q}{2πaA}}$

$\Rightarrow$  $\frac{2R}{a}=\log \left (\frac{1}{1-\frac{Q}{2πaA}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$  R = $\frac{a}{2}$ log $\left (\frac{1}{1-\frac{Q}{2πaA}}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text:
The pitch and the number of divisions,  on the circular scale, for a given screw gauge are 0.5 mm and 100 respectively. When the screw gauge is fully tightened without any object, the zero of its circular scale lies 3 divisions below the mean line. 

The readings of the main scale and the circular scale, for a thin sheet, are 5.5 mm and 48 respectively, the thickness of this sheet is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, 

Least count (LC) = $\frac{Pitch}{no.ofdivisions}$

$\therefore$  LC = $\frac{0.5}{100}$

= 0.5 $\times$ $10^{-2} mm$

Reading = MSR + CSR $-$ positive error 

Given, Main scale reading (MSR) = 5.5 mm

Circular scale reading (CSR) 

= 48 $\times$ 0.5 $\times$ $10^{-2} mm$

= 0.24

As zero of its circular scale lies 3 divisions below the mean line, it means error is positive error. 

$\therefore$  positive error 

= 3 $\times$ 0.5 $\times$ $10^{-2} mm$

= 0.015 mm

$\therefore$  Reading = 5.5 + 0.24 $-$ 0.015

= 5.725 mm
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text: In a car race on straight road, car A takes a time t less than car B at the finish and passes finishing point with a speed '$υ$' more than that of car B. Both the cars start from rest and travel with constant acceleration $a_{1}$ and $a_{2}$ respectively. Then '$υ$' is equal  to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Both cars start from rest and cover the same distance $d$.

Car A: $t_{A}=\sqrt{\dfrac{2d}{a_{1}}}$, $v_{A}=\sqrt{2a_{1}d}$. Car B: $t_{B}=\sqrt{\dfrac{2d}{a_{2}}}$, $v_{B}=\sqrt{2a_{2}d}$.

Time difference:

$t=t_{B}-t_{A}=\sqrt{2d}\left (\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a_{2}}}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a_{1}}}\right )=\sqrt{2d}\dfrac{\sqrt{a_{1}}-\sqrt{a_{2}}}{\sqrt{a_{1}a_{2}}}$

Speed difference:

$v=v_{A}-v_{B}=\sqrt{2d}(\sqrt{a_{1}}-\sqrt{a_{2}})$

Dividing, $\dfrac{v}{t}=\sqrt{a_{1}a_{2}}$, so $v=\sqrt{a_{1}a_{2}}t$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text:
The magnetic field associated with a light wave is given, at the origin, by $B = B_{0}$ [sin(3.14 $\times$ $10^{7})ct + \sin (6.28$ $\times$ $10^{7})ct$]. If this light falls on a silver plate having a work function of 4.7 eV, what will be the maximum kinetic energy of the photo electrons ? 

(Take c = 3 $\times$ $10^{8} ms^{-1}, h = 6.6$ $\times$ $10^{-34}J-s)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that,

$B = B_{0}$[sin (3.14 $\times$ $10^{7}) ct + \sin (6.28$ $\times$ $10^{7}) ct$]

This light wave is non-monochromotic wave as here is two different frequency in the magnetic field.

Given work function ($𝜙$) = 4.7 eV

Question says to find the maximum kinetic energy, so we have to use maximum frequency among the available frequency. 

As, 

$K_{\max } = E_{\max }$ $-$ $𝜙$

Emax = hF

= h $\times$ $\frac{ω}{2π}$

= 6.6 $\times$ $10^{-34}$ $\times$ $\frac{6.28\times 10^{7}\times 3\times 10^{8}}{2π}$

=  6.6$\times$ 3 $\times$ $10^{-19} J$

=  $\frac{6.6\times 3\times 10^{-19}}{1.6\times 10^{-19}}eV$

= 12.375 $eV$

$\therefore$  $K_{\max } = 12.375$ $-$ 4.7

= 7.675 $eV$

$\simeq$  7.7 $eV$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text:
The position co-ordinates of a particle moving in a 3-D coordinate system is given by 

x = a cos$ω$t

y = a sin$ω$t  and

z = a$ω$t

The speed of the particle is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that,

x = a cos $ω$t

y = a sin $ω$t

z = a $ω$t

Velocity in x-direction,

$V_{x} =$ $\frac{dx}{dt}=-aω\sin ωt$

Velocity  in y-direction, 

$V_{y} =$ $\frac{dy}{dt}$ = a $ω$cos $ω$t

Velocity in z-direction, 

$V_{z} =$ $\frac{dz}{dt}$  = a$ω$

Net velocity, 

$\vec{V}$ $= V_{x}\hat{i}$ $+ V_{y}\hat{j}$ $+ V_{z}\widehat{k}$

Speed = $\left |\vec{V}\right |=\sqrt{V_{x}^{2}+V_{y}^{2}+V_{z}^{2}}$

$=\sqrt{a^{2}ω^{2}\sin ^{2}ωt+a^{2}ω^{2}\cos ^{2}ωt+a^{2}ω^{2}}$

$=\sqrt{a^{2}ω^{2}\left (\sin ^{2}ωt+\cos ^{2}ωt\right )+a^{2}ω^{2}}$

$=\sqrt{2a^{2}ω^{2}}$

$=\sqrt{2}aω$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Case 1 : 


[IMG]


Ge need 0.3 V for start conducting and Si need 0.7 V for start conducting. 

So, conduction will be start by Ge. 

Out of 12 V,  0.3V will be consumed by Ge. 

$\therefore$  $V_{01} = 12$ $-$ 0.3  = 11.7 V

Case 2 :


[IMG]


Here as Ge diode is in reverse bias so no conduction will happen through Ge diode 

As Si diode is in forward bias so conduction will happen through Si diode. 

Here Si diode consume 0.7 V.

So, $V_{02} = 12$ $-$ 0.7 = 11.3 V

$\therefore$  Value of $V_{0}$ changes by 

= 11.7 $-$ 11.3 = 0.4 V

text:
A rod of length 50 cm is pivoted at one end. It is raised such that it makes an angle of $30^{o}$  from the horizontal as shown and released from rest. Its angular speed when it passes through the horizontal (in rad $s^{-1})$ will be $(g = 10 ms^{-2})$


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

When this rod move from initial position to final position then, 

Gain in kinetic energy = loss in potential energy 

$\therefore$  $\frac{1}{2}Iω^{2}$ = mgh

$\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{ml^{2}}{3}\right )$ $ω^{2}$ = mg$\left (\frac{l}{2}\sin 30^{\circ }\right )$

$\Rightarrow$  $ω^{2}$ = $\frac{3g}{2l}$

$\Rightarrow$  $ω$ = $\sqrt{\frac{3g}{2l}}$

$\Rightarrow$  $ω$ = $\sqrt{\frac{3\times 10}{2\times 0.5}}$

$\Rightarrow$  $ω$ = $\sqrt{30}$ rad/sec

text:
In the given circuit the internal resistance of the 18 V cell is negligible. If $R_{1} = 400$ $\Omega$, $R_{3} = 100$ $\Omega$ and $R_{4} = 500$ $\Omega$ and the reading of an ideal voltmeter across $R_{4}$ is 5V, then the value of $R_{2}$ will be : 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Voltage across resistance $R_{4} = 5 V$

$\therefore$   $IR_{4} = 5 V$

$\Rightarrow$   500 $\times$ I = 5

$\Rightarrow$   I = $\frac{1}{100}$ A

$\therefore$   Voltage across resistor $R_{3} =$ $\frac{1}{100}(100)$ = 1 V

$\therefore$   Total drop in resistance $R_{3}$ and $R_{4} = 5 + 1 = 6V$

So, voltage across $R_{2}$ resistance is also 6V as $R_{3}, R_{4}$ and $R_{2}$ are in parallel

$\therefore$   Voltage across $R_{1}$ resistor = 18 $-$ 6 = 12 V

$\therefore$   Current through $R_{1}$ resistor = $\frac{12}{400}$ = $\frac{3}{100}$ A

$\therefore$   Current through $R_{2}$ resistor 

= $\frac{3}{100}-\frac{1}{100}$

=  $\frac{2}{100}$ A

$\therefore$   $\left (\frac{2}{100}\right )$  $R_{2} = 6$

$\Rightarrow$   $R_{2} = 300$ $\Omega$
